candidates.label: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma
missing_or_uncertain: Subtype confirmation (e.g., FOXO1 fusion) not performed

candidates.label: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma
missing_or_uncertain: Molecular testing for FOXO1 fusion not done

candidates.label: Spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma
missing_or_uncertain: Histology shows small round blue cells, not spindle cells

candidates.label: Ectomesenchymoma
missing_or_uncertain: Neural markers not tested, but SOX-10 negative

response.rationale: The IHC profile (positive MyoD1, myogenin, vimentin, desmin) is highly specific for skeletal muscle differentiation, strongly supporting rhabdomyosarcoma. The clinical presentation (adolescent, slow-growing skin lesion) and histology (small round blue cells) are consistent. Embryonal subtype is more common in this age group and location, while alveolar is less common but possible. Other small round blue cell tumors are excluded by negative markers (CD45, CK, SOX-10, etc.). The 8-month development favors embryonal over alveolar, which tends to be more aggressive.
